insights.title: Retail inflation is 5.54%
insights.text: In September 2026 CPI inflation was above the 4% target but inside the 2-6% band that the Government has set for the RBI (1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031).

insights.title: Real policy rate −0.29 pp
insights.text: The repo rate of 5.50% minus CPI inflation of 5.54% in September 2026. A negative real rate means prices are rising faster than the policy rate.

insights.title: Wholesale above retail by 5.85 pp
insights.text: WPI inflation was 11.39% against CPI's 5.54% in September 2026. Producer and trader prices rising faster than shop prices is a cost pressure that can reach retail prices later.

insights.title: GDP grew 7.82% in real terms
insights.text: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): 10.33% at current prices, so prices across the whole economy (the GDP deflator) rose about 2.51%.

insights.title: Reserves US$721.0 bn
insights.text: As on 16 October 2026: down US$5.01 bn in the week and up US$18.74 bn on a year earlier; gold is 14.7% of the total.

insights.title: Credit faster than deposits
insights.text: Bank credit grew 18.2% and deposits 16.7% in the year to 15 October 2026.

insights.title: Unemployment 5.0%
insights.text: September 2026, people aged 15 and above; 15.2% for those aged 15-29.

targetWatch.rule: If CPI inflation averages above 6% or below 2% for three quarters in a row, the RBI must report to the Government why, and what it will do.

cpi.label: CPI inflation
cpi.what: Retail prices: what households pay, year on year.
cpi.note: MoSPI's published inflation rate, base 2024 = 100: the back series for 2013-2024 and the current series from January 2026. For the 12 months of 2025 (the new series' first year, for which MoSPI publishes no rate) the change is worked out from the current series' index against the back series' index for the same month, both on base 2024 (published indices are rounded to two decimals, so such a figure can differ from MoSPI's own by 0.01 percentage point).

wpi.label: WPI inflation
wpi.what: Wholesale prices: what producers and traders pay, year on year.
wpi.note: MoSPI publishes the wholesale index, not an inflation rate: each month is the index against the same month a year earlier, always within one base (2011-12 = 100 until December 2023; 2022-23 = 100 from January 2024).

gdp.label: GDP growth
gdp.what: Real GDP (constant prices), the quarter against the same quarter a year earlier.
gdp.note: Quarterly GDP from the National Statistics Office: real (constant prices) and nominal (current prices), each quarter against the same quarter a year earlier, within one base year (2011-12, then 2022-23 once it has a year of history).

gdp_nominal.label: Nominal GDP growth
gdp_nominal.what: GDP at current prices, year on year.

iip.label: Industrial production
iip.what: Index of Industrial Production, growth year on year.
iip.note: MoSPI's published growth rate of the Index of Industrial Production (base 2022-23; base 2011-12 before it).

unemployment.label: Unemployment rate
unemployment.what: Persons aged 15 and above, rural and urban, current weekly status.
unemployment.note: Periodic Labour Force Survey, monthly estimate (published from January 2025), current weekly status.

repo.label: RBI repo rate
repo.what: The policy rate: what banks pay to borrow from the RBI overnight.
repo.note: The rate in force at each month end, from every RBI policy decision since April 2016; today's figure is read from rbi.org.in.

real_rate.label: Real repo rate
real_rate.source: Derived: RBI repo rate minus CPI inflation
real_rate.what: The repo rate minus CPI inflation of the same month.

fx_reserves.label: Forex reserves
fx_reserves.what: Foreign exchange reserves: currency assets, gold, SDRs and the IMF position.
fx_reserves.note: Month-end reserves from the RBI's tables (as republished by MoSPI), and weekly figures from the RBI's Weekly Statistical Supplement from the week they were first read; a weekly release also states the change against end-March and a year earlier, from which those two weeks are added.

usdinr.label: Rupee per US dollar
usdinr.what: Reference rate, monthly average (latest: today's FBIL reference rate).
usdinr.note: Monthly average of the reference rate (RBI tables, as republished by MoSPI), then the daily FBIL reference rate shown on rbi.org.in from the day it was first read.

credit_yoy.label: Bank credit growth
credit_yoy.what: Scheduled commercial banks' credit in India, year on year.
credit_yoy.note: Scheduled commercial banks, business in India, as the RBI's weekly statistical supplement states it, from the week it was first read.
